prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of Labour Party Manifesto 2024 (≤500 words)

Core message
- “Time for change”: end Conservative “chaos,” restore stability, rebuild national confidence, and put politics in service of working people.
- Mission-driven government with five long-term missions: growth, clean energy, safer streets, opportunity for every child, and an NHS fit for the future.
- Strong foundations: national security, secure borders, and economic stability under tough fiscal rules.

First steps
- Economic stability: strict fiscal rules; OBR oversight; no rises in NI, Income Tax rates or VAT.
- NHS: 40,000 extra weekly appointments (evenings/weekends), funded by tackling tax avoidance/non-dom regime.
- Borders: new Border Security Command; counter-terror style powers against smuggling gangs; end Rwanda scheme.
- Energy: create publicly owned Great British Energy (funded by strengthened windfall tax).
- Crime: more neighbourhood policing, tougher antisocial penalties, youth hubs.
- Education: 6,500 new teachers (funded by ending private school tax breaks).

Economy and growth
- Pro-business, pro-worker “securonomics”; industrial strategy with a statutory Industrial Strategy Council.
- National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to crowd in private capital: ports, gigafactories, steel, CCUS, green hydrogen.
- Planning reform to build 1.5m homes; new towns; brownfield-first; strategic “grey belt” release with “golden rules.”
- Devolution: Local Growth Plans; wider powers for mayors; multi-year council funding.
- Business taxation: cap corporation tax at 25% for the parliament; permanent full expensing; replace business rates in England.
- Infrastructure: 10-year strategy; new National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority; push for full gigabit and 5G by 2030; rail brought into public ownership as contracts expire; bus franchising and municipal ownership enabled.
- Work: New Deal for Working People—ban exploitative zero-hours, end fire-and-rehire, day-one rights, Single Enforcement Body; minimum wage to reflect cost of living and remove adult age bands.
- Immigration: reduce net migration; link visas to skills plans; tougher enforcement against abuse.

Clean energy and environment
- Clean power by 2030: double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; support nuclear; no new North Sea exploration licences; ban fracking.
- Great British Energy (£8.3bn) to co-invest and scale local power; British Jobs Bonus to anchor supply chains.
- Warm Homes Plan (£6.6bn): upgrade 5m homes; tighter PRS standards by 2030.
- Water: special measures for failing companies; tougher fines/bonus bans; independent outlet monitoring.
- Nature and farming: new National River Walks, three National Forests; 50% of public sector food local/high-standard; end badger cull; stronger animal welfare (ban trail hunting, trophy imports, puppy smuggling, snares).

Crime and justice
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee; Respect Orders; tougher shoplifting/enforcement.
- Halve knife crime in a decade; ban zombie-style weapons; mandatory interventions for knife possession; Young Futures hubs nationwide.
- Violence against women and girls: specialist rape units in every force; fast-track courts; stronger stalking/spiking laws; better victim support.
- Prisons: build capacity; cut reoffending; probation governance review; Hillsborough Law; address historic injustices.

Opportunity, housing, and services
- Childcare: 3,000 school-based nurseries; review parental leave.
- Schools: curriculum/assessment review; free breakfast clubs for all primaries; mental health support in every school; SEND inclusion; leadership and inspection reform.
- Skills: Skills England; Growth & Skills Levy; Technical Excellence Colleges; guarantee training/apprenticeship/support for all 18–21s; HE funding reform.
- Housing: end Section 21 evictions; raise private rented standards (extend Awaab’s Law); reform leasehold toward commonhold; major boost to social/affordable homes; mortgage guarantee for first-time buyers.
- Health: double CT/MRI scanners; modernise estates; family doctor continuity; community pharmacy prescribing; Dentistry Rescue Plan (700k urgent appointments, contract reform); National Care Service with Fair Pay Agreement; 8,500 new mental health staff; strong public health measures (smoking/vaping, junk food ads, energy drinks).

Politics and the world
- Clean up politics: independent Ethics and Integrity Commission; ban MPs’ paid consultancy roles; modernise Commons; Lords reform (end hereditary peers; retirement at 80) and consult on replacement chamber; votes at 16; reset with devolved governments.
- Foreign policy: unshakeable NATO and nuclear deterrent; Strategic Defence Review; defence industrial strategy; steadfast support for Ukraine (including using frozen Russian assets); AUKUS; pragmatic China approach; improve EU relations (security pact, trade barriers, vet and qualifications deals); targeted trade strategy; Clean Power Alliance; rebuild UK development leadership and restore 0.7% when fiscal conditions allow.
